title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is entire block rejected if ANY transaction exceeds gas cap?
state_context: Prysm (OffchainLabs/prysm) is a consensus layer (CL) client. It has no txpool, no per-transaction gas limit validation, and no EIP-7825 constants. Execution payload validation is delegated to the EL via engine_newPayloadVX. beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go ValidatePayload() checks only randao mix and timestamp; ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes() checks only parent hash.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm has no abstract state domain covering per-transaction gas limits. The ExecutionPayload is treated as an opaque blob at the CL level. State variables tracked by Prysm for execution payloads are: block hash, parent hash, randao mix, timestamp, gas_limit (block-level aggregate), gas_used, and KZG commitments — none are per-transaction fields. The value 16777216 in Prysm appears only as HistoricalRootsLimit (SSZ list size cap), not as a TxGasCap. No MaxTxGasLimit, TxGasCap, or EIP7825 constant exists in Prysm's production code.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No cache of per-transaction gas limits exists in Prysm. The beacon state's latest_execution_payload_header contains only block-level gas_limit and gas_used fields. No transaction-level fields are cached or inspected.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable. Since Prysm performs no per-transaction gas limit validation, there are no shared mutable state variables related to EIP-7825 gas cap enforcement that could be subject to race conditions within Prysm.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No exploit path exists within Prysm for this property. Symbolic execution shows that the full ExecutionPayload, including its Transactions field, is passed unmodified to the EL via engine_newPayloadVX (beacon-chain/execution/engine_client.go NotifyNewPayload). Prysm returns VALID only when the EL returns VALID status. A block with an oversized transaction (gasLimit=16777217) would be rejected or accepted based entirely on the EL's behavior. Prysm never interposes on that decision.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Not applicable. No TOCTOU window exists because Prysm performs no per-transaction gas limit check at any point in the block processing pipeline.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The check_id property (CHK-0005: entire block rejected if ANY transaction exceeds gas cap) is architecturally unreachable as a Prysm responsibility. The Engine API call chain is: P2P receive beacon block -> beacon-chain/sync/validate_beacon_blocks.go (CL validation only: BLS signatures, structure, KZG commitments) -> blockchain/execution_engine.go notifyNewPayload -> engine_client.go NewPayload (engine_newPayloadVX) -> EL validates and responds VALID/INVALID. Prysm only acts on the EL's response.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No attack surface within Prysm for this property. EIP-7825 per-transaction gas cap enforcement is solely an execution layer responsibility. An attacker wishing to exploit missing gas cap enforcement would need to target the EL component, not Prysm.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'entire block is rejected if any transaction exceeds gas cap' cannot be proven or disproven at the Prysm level because Prysm has no code implementing this check. The invariant is delegated to the EL. Prysm's behavior: accept whatever validity decision the EL returns via engine_newPayloadVX. If the EL enforces EIP-7825 correctly, the invariant holds system-wide. If the EL does not, Prysm cannot compensate.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Engine API delegation: Prysm calls s.cfg.ExecutionEngineCaller.NewPayload(ctx, payload, ...) and relies on EL INVALID response to reject blocks (beacon-chain/blockchain/execution_engine.go:271).
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: The delegation pattern is architecturally correct for the CL/EL separation of concerns defined by the Engine API specification. Prysm is not responsible for per-transaction gas limit validation.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: EIP-7825 per-transaction gas cap enforcement is explicitly an execution layer concern. Prysm is a consensus layer client. It has no txpool, no per-transaction gas limit code, and no relevant constants (16777216 as TxGasCap does not exist in any non-SSZ Prysm Go file). The architectural pattern of delegating execution payload validity to the EL via engine_newPayloadVX is correct and intended. This item is out-of-scope for Prysm.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: This check should be redirected to the execution layer client (e.g., go-ethereum/nitro/reth) used alongside Prysm. No changes are needed in Prysm.

title: Verify Post-Condition: All transactions in valid blocks have gasLimit <= 16777216?
state_context: Prysm is a CL client. The ExecutionPayload.Transactions field is an opaque [][]byte at the CL level — raw RLP-encoded transaction bytes that Prysm never decodes. beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go ValidatePayload() only checks randao mix and timestamp; no transaction content inspection occurs.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: This post-condition (all transactions in validated blocks have gasLimit <= 16777216) requires Prysm to inspect transaction-level fields within ExecutionPayload. Code examination of beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go shows ValidatePayload() checks only randao mix and timestamp; ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes() checks only parent hash. Neither function inspects the Transactions slice contents. The ExecutionPayload.Transactions field is an opaque [][]byte at the CL level — raw RLP-encoded transaction bytes that Prysm never decodes.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: The beacon state's latest_execution_payload_header contains gas_limit (block aggregate) and gas_used, not per-transaction gas limits. No transaction-level state is maintained in Prysm.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable. Prysm's block processing pipeline processes blocks sequentially per fork-choice lock. Even with concurrency, since no per-transaction gas check exists, there is no relevant race condition.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Constructing an exploit of this property within Prysm is impossible because Prysm never decodes or inspects individual transaction bytes within an ExecutionPayload. The Transactions field type is [][]byte (raw bytes). To check per-transaction gasLimit, Prysm would need to RLP-decode each transaction and inspect the gasLimit field — code that does not exist in the Prysm codebase (confirmed by comprehensive grep for MaxTxGasLimit, TxGasCap, EIP7825, and the constant 16777216 in non-SSZ contexts).

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Block acceptance in Prysm is determined by the EL's VALID/INVALID response to engine_newPayloadVX. If the EL returns VALID for a block containing an oversized transaction (which would be an EL bug), Prysm would accept that block and cache the payload header — but this is an EL failure, not a Prysm failure. The post-condition verification point is architecturally unreachable within Prysm.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: The attack surface for this property is entirely within the execution layer. Prysm trusts the EL's validity determination as specified by the Engine API protocol.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The post-condition invariant is not Prysm's responsibility to enforce. Prysm correctly implements the Engine API contract: it submits payloads to the EL for validation and propagates the VALID/INVALID result. This architectural pattern is the intended design in the Ethereum proof-of-stake specification.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Full delegation to EL via engine_newPayloadVX (engine_client.go). EL returns INVALID for non-compliant blocks; Prysm marks them invalid.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient from Prysm's architectural perspective. Prysm is not the component responsible for decoding and validating individual transaction gas limits.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: This post-condition (per-transaction gasLimit <= 16777216 for all transactions in validated blocks) is an execution layer invariant. Prysm, as a CL client, never inspects individual transaction contents within ExecutionPayload. The transactions are opaque RLP-encoded bytes at the CL level. This is out-of-scope for Prysm.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Audit the execution layer client for EIP-7825 compliance. No changes are warranted in Prysm.

title: Verify Defense-in-Depth: Are both txpool and block validation enforcing gas cap independently?
state_context: Prysm has no txpool. Grep for 'txpool', 'TxPool', 'mempool' in Prysm returns only 3 files, all for end-to-end testing of external EL nodes (testing/endtoend/components/eth1/). Prysm's block validation (validate_beacon_blocks.go) checks BLS signatures, beacon block structure, slot validity, proposer correctness, KZG commitment counts — no transaction gas limit checks.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: This defense-in-depth check requires two independent enforcement layers: txpool and block validation. Prysm has neither for per-transaction gas limits. No txpool exists in Prysm. Prysm's block validation (validate_beacon_blocks.go) performs CL-level structural checks: BLS signatures, beacon block structure, slot validity, proposer checks, KZG commitments — no transaction gas limit checks whatsoever.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: Not applicable. No txpool state or per-transaction gas limit validation state exists in Prysm.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable. Prysm has no implementation of the defense-in-depth layers being audited.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: This check asks whether both txpool and block validation independently enforce EIP-7825. From Prysm's perspective, neither layer exists. There are no symbolic paths through Prysm code that enforce per-transaction gas caps at either the txpool stage (non-existent in Prysm) or the block validation stage. The question is entirely about EL-internal architecture.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The defense-in-depth property describes EL-internal architecture (txpool + block validation). Prysm participates in the pipeline only as a relay: it passes execution payloads to the EL via engine_newPayloadVX and receives VALID/INVALID. The CL has no visibility into whether EL enforcement uses defense-in-depth or a single layer.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No Prysm attack surface exists for this property. The entire question is about EL-internal validation architecture.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant (txpool and block validation both enforce gas cap independently) does not apply to Prysm. Prysm has no txpool. The closest Prysm has to 'block validation' for execution payloads is the delegation to the EL via engine_newPayloadVX. Independent enforcement within Prysm is architecturally impossible and would violate the CL/EL separation of concerns.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: This check is entirely about EL-internal defense-in-depth (txpool + block validation both enforcing EIP-7825 gas cap). Prysm has no txpool and no per-transaction gas limit validation. This is categorically out-of-scope for the Prysm CL client.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Audit the EL client (go-ethereum/nitro/reth) for defense-in-depth EIP-7825 enforcement. This check does not apply to Prysm.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is cap value 16777216 identical at txpool and block validation?
state_context: The value 16777216 in Prysm appears exclusively as HistoricalRootsLimit (SSZ list size cap) and in an unrelated byte encoding test (encoding/bytesutil/integers_test.go). It does not appear as a TxGasCap, MaxTxGasLimit, or EIP-7825 constant in any Prysm production Go file. No per-transaction gas limit constants exist in config/params/ package.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: This check requires that the constant 16777216 (2^24, EIP-7825 per-transaction gas cap) be consistent between txpool and block validation. Code search confirms that 16777216 appears in Prysm exclusively in: (1) HistoricalRootsLimit SSZ field size cap, (2) an unrelated byte encoding test. No occurrence of 16777216 as a TxGasCap, MaxTxGasLimit, or EIP-7825 constant exists anywhere in Prysm's non-test, non-SSZ production code.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No gas cap constant state exists in Prysm's config/params package or anywhere else relevant to per-transaction gas limits.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No symbolic path exists where Prysm compares or uses 16777216 as a gas cap constant for transactions. The only transaction-related size constant in Prysm is MaxBytesPerTxLength (1073741824 bytes, for SSZ deserialization bounds checking in api/server/structs/ and config/fieldparams/mainnet.go:22) — this is a byte-length limit for SSZ encoding, not a gas limit for EIP-7825.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Constant inconsistency within Prysm for EIP-7825 gas caps cannot occur because the constant does not exist in Prysm in the relevant context. The property of consistent gas cap constants between txpool and block validation is an EL concern.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No attack surface within Prysm. The EIP-7825 constant consistency must be verified in EL client source code.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant (gas cap constant identical at txpool and block validation) is trivially satisfied in Prysm because neither component nor the constant exists in Prysm in the relevant context. There is nothing to be inconsistent.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The EIP-7825 gas cap constant (16777216 as a TxGasCap or MaxTxGasLimit) does not exist in Prysm. The value 16777216 appears only as HistoricalRootsLimit (a beacon state SSZ structure limit). Both txpool and per-transaction block validation are EL responsibilities. This check is entirely out-of-scope for Prysm.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Search for this constant inconsistency in the EL client. In Prysm, no action is required.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Can rejected transactions leak into block building via race conditions?
state_context: Prysm's block building path: beacon-chain/rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/validator/proposer_execution_payload.go calls ForkchoiceUpdated (to instruct EL to build block) then GetPayload (to retrieve EL-built block). Prysm has no txpool-to-builder pipeline. Transaction selection, ordering, gas limit validation, and inclusion decisions are entirely performed within the EL. Prysm caches payloadID (beacon-chain/cache/payload_id.go) as a reference to the EL-built payload, not transaction data.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: This check concerns a TOCTOU race condition between txpool validation and block building. Block building in Prysm means calling engine_forkchoiceUpdatedVX with payload attributes, then engine_getPayloadVX to retrieve the built block. Prysm has no txpool-to-builder pipeline. Transaction selection, ordering, gas limit validation, and inclusion decisions are all performed entirely within the EL during the GetPayload call. Prysm merely requests the pre-built payload from the EL. The payloadID cache in Prysm is a reference to the EL-built payload, not transaction data.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: Prysm caches the payloadID (beacon-chain/cache/payload_id.go) returned by ForkchoiceUpdated — this is a reference to the EL-built payload, not transaction data. No transaction-level state is managed in Prysm during block building. No TOCTOU race is possible in Prysm for this property.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No TOCTOU race is possible within Prysm for this property because Prysm's block-building pipeline contains no per-transaction gas limit validation step. The pipeline is: forkchoiceUpdated (requests EL to build block) -> getPayload (retrieves EL-built block) -> propose beacon block containing the EL payload. At no point does Prysm inspect or filter individual transactions.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Constructing a TOCTOU exploit within Prysm for transaction gas limit enforcement is impossible because Prysm performs no gas limit check on transactions at any step. The only concurrent access risk in Prysm's block building path is the payloadID cache (shared state across validator goroutines), but this caches block references, not transaction data. Even high-frequency submission of oversized transactions during block building would not affect Prysm's behavior — the EL handles all transaction filtering.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Not applicable within Prysm. Any TOCTOU race in transaction filtering exists entirely within the EL's txpool-to-block-builder pipeline.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The txpool-to-builder pipeline race condition is an EL-internal concern. Prysm's block building path (proposer_execution_payload.go) demonstrates that Prysm only calls ForkchoiceUpdated to signal block building intent and GetPayload to retrieve the result. No transaction filtering or gas cap enforcement occurs between these two calls within Prysm.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No Prysm attack surface. The TOCTOU race between txpool rejection and block building is entirely within EL-internal execution. An attacker would need to target the EL's txpool and block-building subsystem.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant (rejected transactions cannot leak into block building via race conditions) is enforced entirely by the EL. Prysm's block building abstraction (getLocalPayload -> ForkchoiceUpdated -> GetPayload) correctly delegates all transaction management to the EL. No invariant relating to per-transaction gas limits needs to be maintained within Prysm.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Full delegation to EL via engine_forkchoiceUpdatedVX and engine_getPayloadVX. Prysm never selects or filters transactions (proposer_execution_payload.go).
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Architecturally correct. Prysm's guard (delegation to EL) is appropriate for a CL client. Adding txpool-level transaction filtering to Prysm would violate the Engine API separation of concerns.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The txpool-to-block-builder TOCTOU race condition for EIP-7825 gas cap enforcement is entirely an EL concern. Prysm has no txpool and no per-transaction gas limit validation in its block building pipeline. The proposer path (proposer_execution_payload.go) only calls ForkchoiceUpdated and GetPayload — the EL builds the block contents. This is out-of-scope for Prysm.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Audit the EL client's txpool-to-block-builder synchronization for race conditions that could allow oversized transactions to bypass EIP-7825 enforcement. No changes are needed in Prysm.
